_schema.feast: MM-DD fixed feast date (the date hook, same as founder birth/death hooks)
_schema.name: primary saint name
_schema.phrases: list of ALL-CAPS phrases to run through the 8 ciphers into the day pool (names, titles, patronages, places, story terms)
_schema.death_year: year of death (enters pool as-is; anniversary span = current year - death_year, used as-is only, NO factorization per rule)
_schema.death_date: MM-DD if known, null if not
_schema.age: age at death if known (enters pool as-is)
_schema.patronage: human-readable patronage list for narrative routing
_schema.narratives: story keys for routing to players/teams
_schema.blurb: pre-baked story summary (written once, costs nothing daily)

_rules.no_factorization: numbers count as-is or not at all — never break a number apart to manufacture a hit
_rules.echo_tier: same-day landings = full weight; +/-1 day = echo tier (weaker)
_rules.strongest_stamp: narrative carrier + number carrier converging on one player

entries.name: Clare of Assisi
entries.blurb: Follower of Francis, founded the Poor Clares. On her deathbed she saw Mass projected on her wall — why she is patron of television.

entries.name: Jane Frances de Chantal
entries.blurb: Widowed young, founded the Visitation order with Francis de Sales. Patroness of widows and the forgotten.

entries.name: Pontian and Hippolytus
entries.blurb: Pope Pontian (#18, first to resign) and Hippolytus (first antipope) — rivals exiled to the Sardinian mines who reconciled and died together, 235 AD. Old calendar adds Cassian of Imola, the teacher stabbed to death by his own students' styluses.

entries.name: Maximilian Kolbe
entries.blurb: Franciscan friar who volunteered to die in place of a stranger at Auschwitz, 1941. The ultimate substitution story — one man stepping in for another.

entries.name: Assumption of Mary
patronage: holy day of obligation — highest-weight Marian feast of the year
entries.blurb: Mary taken body and soul into heaven — the biggest feast of August. Elevation is the theme: rising, call-ups, career peaks.

entries.name: Stephen of Hungary
entries.blurb: First King of Hungary, crowned in 1000 AD, founded the Hungarian state and church. A king's day — crowns and Stephen names.

entries.name: Bernard of Clairvaux
entries.blurb: Cistercian abbot, the 'honey-sweet doctor' whose preaching launched the Second Crusade. Bees and honey are his signs.

entries.name: Pius X
entries.blurb: Pope who died as World War I broke out, 1914. Lowered the age for first communion — a day for firsts.

entries.name: Rose of Lima
entries.blurb: First canonized saint of the Americas, a Peruvian mystic who died at 31. Roses, gardens, and Latin America carry her day.

entries.name: Bartholomew the Apostle
entries.blurb: Apostle martyred by being flayed alive — patron of everyone who works leather. The leather day: gloves, the ball itself.

entries.name: Louis IX of France
narratives: SAINT LOUIS — the city, the Cardinals
entries.blurb: The crusader king of France who died on crusade in 1270 — the saint the city of St. Louis is named for. Cardinals games carry his day automatically.

entries.name: Monica
entries.blurb: Mother of Augustine, prayed 17 years for her son's conversion and lived to see it. The long-awaited-payoff day.

entries.name: Augustine of Hippo
narratives: brewers — Milwaukee carries the day by name
entries.blurb: The wild-living convert who became the Church's greatest mind, bishop of Hippo, died 430. Brewers games carry his patronage by name.

entries.name: Beheading of John the Baptist
patronage: the martyrdom feast of the Forerunner
narratives: beheading (closers losing heads, aces knocked out early)
the dance that cost a head (showboating punished)
entries.blurb: The Forerunner beheaded at Herod's banquet after Salome's dance. The severed-head day — sudden cuts, early exits.
